## Command history

- Keep every finished command with its output, folder, session, time and exit result, and search it across all sessions with Ctrl+Shift+H. History is off until you turn it on in Settings or on the Welcome screen.
- Filter by host, folder, exit result, session, time or day (the calendar marks days with history), jump between matches in the output, insert a command at the prompt, or open its session.
- When a command has run more than once on the same host, Compare with Previous shows what changed between runs, unified or side by side, with changed words marked and F7 to step between changes. Timestamps are ignored by default, and numbers can be too.
- History stays on this PC in `history.db`. Set how many days to keep, clear it from Settings, or opt individual sessions out. Deleted history is removed from the disk.

## Settings

- Settings now opens as a tab instead of a dialog, with General, Recording, Highlighting, Agents and Keyboard Shortcuts sections. Changes save as you make them and apply to every open window, including theme and font changes.
- "Confirm before closing active sessions" and "Write crash reports" are now in Settings > General.
- Add "Start resesh when I sign in to Windows" to Settings > General. It respects the Startup apps switch in Task Manager.

## Taskbar

- Right-click resesh on the taskbar for a jump list of pinned and recent sessions and a New Window task.
- Opening a session while resesh is running now opens it in the window you used last and brings that window forward.

## Telnet

- Choose a text encoding per telnet session: Automatic (UTF-8, switching to CP437 for BBS and ANSI art), UTF-8 or CP437.
- Optionally report 80 x 25 to BBS servers while the tab keeps its real size.

## Fixes and polish

- Adding, deleting, moving or renaming sessions no longer scrolls the session tree back to the top.
- Remaining tabs no longer flash at a narrower width when you close a tab.
- Menu items are disabled when they don't apply, and a shortcut that can't run passes its key to the terminal.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/bpbp-boop/resesh/compare/v0.15.0...v0.16.0)
